368807.reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), high effort, no child agents

target.source: Vercesi, Barta, Gambardella, Gualandi, Mastrolilli, arXiv:2506.10671v1 (only version as of 2026-11-02T05:23Z), Conjecture 1, p. 14
target.statement: For each x vertex [of P_ASEP^n], N(x) contains at least one tour.
target.claim_under_review: x* = X/4 (19 support arcs) is a vertex of P_ASEP^8 adjacent to no tour; Conjecture 1 fails at n = 8

findings: Formulas (2)-(4), (6) read in the PDF: x in R^m, m = n(n-1), arcs i != j, in- and out-degree = 1, x(delta(S)) >= 1 for all S with 2 <= |S| <= n-2, delta(S) = {(i,j): i in S, j not in S}, x >= 0. Lean arcPolytope (ASEPArcs) and polytope (ASEPDefs, zero-diagonal matrix form used by the source in Sec. 3) render this exactly; reviewer's own RV.P (different encoding, no natural subtraction) is proved equal to arcPolytope n for every n.

Definition 3: N(x) = set of all vertices adjacent to x. Lemma 7's proof: y shares exactly r(n)-1 linearly independent tight constraints with x, i.e. rank-based ordinary adjacency (edge of the polytope). Sec. 5.2 and Figure 6 call the graph the 'polyhedral graph' (Definition 8: vertices and edges of the polyhedron). Ordinary adjacency is the intended meaning.

Pivot reading: N'(x) = Pivoting(x,T) is explicitly a SUBSET of N(x), and a nondegenerate simplex pivot moves along an edge, while every edge at x is reached from some feasible basis of x; so the pivot neighbourhood of a degenerate vertex equals the ordinary neighbourhood and cannot be larger. Orbit-representative reading: Lemma 7 makes N equivariant and tours form one orbit (Lemma 4), so representatives change nothing. No reasonable reading rescues the conjecture.

Reviewer's exact controls with ordinary adjacency reproduce the source's own neighbourhood data: n = 4 has 12 vertices, each tour adjacent to all vertices but one, each fractional vertex adjacent to 5 of the 6 tours; n = 5 has 384 vertices in 5 orbits (60, 120, 60, 120, 24) with tight-set counts 6, 4, 4, 4, 10 as in Table 2; |N(x)| = 28 for (a), 23 for (d) and 148 for tours (e), as in Table 2; every vertex has a neighbour in every other orbit, and only (d) and (e) have self-orbit neighbours, as stated in Sec. 5.2.

n range: the conjecture states no n; it follows the n = 4, 5, 6 tests and is motivated by obtaining the full V-description of the polytope in general. The Lean form for every n >= 4 is faithful; any reading whose n-range contains 8 is refuted. The MathDB raw statement ('for every vertex x, N(x) contains at least one tour', neighbourhood 'in the vertex structure considered by the paper') matches.
objections: A-1 (minor, source-internal, not affecting the verdict): Table 2 prints |N(x)| = 20 for orbit (b) (1/3, 2/3 entries) and 28 for orbit (c) (1/2 entries, 4 tight sets), but exact ordinary adjacency gives 11 and 20. Rank-based and rank-free combinatorial counts agree, and a tour/fractional edge double count is consistent (3000 = 24 x 125). The other three cells and all qualitative statements match, so this looks like a table error (the printed values look shifted by one row), not a broader neighbourhood notion; the source defines no notion that would give larger counts. The manuscript should mention this without overclaiming.

A-2 (minor): Optimization Online lists the paper as 'Published 2024/03/28, Updated 2025/06/15'. The 2024 version (main-1.pdf) now returns 404, so it could not be checked whether Conjecture 1 was already stated in March 2024 (MathDB records first_stated_year 2025). This affects chronology only.

findings: Reviewer's own stdlib-only exact code (scripts/rv_asep.py, fraction-free integer elimination): x* feasible; 19 support arcs; min positive entry 1/4; the 8 tight cuts are exactly {0,3},{4,6},{0,3,7},{4,5,6},{0,1,2,3,7},{1,2,4,5,6},{0,1,2,3,5,7},{1,2,4,5,6,7}; min non-tight cut value 5/4; vertex rank 56 = m (vertex).

All 5040 tours (all cyclic orders 0,p1..p7): rank of the common tight system <= 54 for every tour; histogram {44:213, 45:590, 46:913, 47:958, 48:846, 49:626, 50:430, 51:232, 52:123, 53:82, 54:27}, identical to the author's Python and JavaScript; 0 adjacent tours.

Structurally different second check (scripts/rv_perturb.py): exact Fraction Gauss-Jordan nullspace (min nullity 2 = face dimension >= 2), rank mod 1000003 agrees with the rational rank for every tour, and for each of the 5040 tours an explicit rational direction v not parallel to x*-T with z +- eps v verified feasible against ALL 16 + 56 + 238 constraints exactly. 5040/5040 non-faces witnessed.

Perturbation logic of the writeup checked by hand and in Lean (ASEPSound.not_extreme_of_dir): at z = (x*+T)/2 every non-tight constraint has slack >= 1/8 (entries 0 or >= 1/4, cut values 1 or >= 5/4, T is 0/1 with integral crossing counts >= 1); sum|v| <= 64 bounds every partial double sum, so |v/512| changes are <= 1/8; J-tight constraints are preserved by v; an extreme segment would force v to be parallel to x* - T, contradicting the 2x2 minor. Correct.
n = 4 control (source Example 1): vertex, adjacent to 5 of 6 tours (perturbation code fails exactly on those 5, as expected).

n = 7 probe (optional, NOT exhaustive): collapsing either tight 2-set of x* (source Lemma 8) gives feasible non-vertices of P_ASEP^7 (rank 41 < 42); 21 random-LP fractional vertices of P_ASEP^7 each have >= 4 adjacent tours. Minimality of n = 8 is open; nothing in the claim depends on it.

Fresh byte-identical copy of the 21 proof modules plus PermOrder (lean-build/src-sha256.txt). Built one module at a time in dependency order with lean 4.34.1 (commit 5045d005) -j1 -DwarningAsError=true against the pinned prebuilt mathlib d13f23b7 oleans, sanitised env (env -i, LEAN_PATH only pinned packages plus the review build dir), each under systemd scope MemoryMax=6G and the reviewer's own private-RSS watchdog: all rc 0; peak private RSS 4917 MiB (ASEPCover); max CPU 20.4 s per build.
leanchecker (non-fresh) rc 0 on all 21 proof modules; leanchecker --fresh rc 0 on ASEPData, ASEPCheck and ASEPDefs (56.8 s, 70.5 s, 100.1 s CPU).

Full declaration audit (lean-review/RVAudit.lean -> outputs/lean-decl-audit.jsonl): 300 local constants (187 theorems, 110 defs, 1 structure with ctor and recursor). Every def and theorem has value? = true; no axioms, no opaque declarations, no implemented_by or extern. Every constant's collectAxioms is a subset of {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. An independent body walk over the 12354-constant transitive closure, which ignores olean-cached axiom data, reaches only those three axioms and has no missing constants.

Only flagged items: ASEP.digs._unsafe_rec and ASEP.triples._unsafe_rec are compiler-generated partial auxiliaries. They appear in NO endpoint closure (RVClosure); the kernel also forbids safe declarations from referencing partial ones.

Endpoint closures (6 author endpoints plus 2 reviewer theorems) contain no sorryAx, ofReduceBool, ofReduceNat or trustCompiler, and no unsafe or partial constant; each reaches all 48 chunkK_ok theorems and certs_cover. A textual scan of the sources finds no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, ofReduceBool, implemented_by, extern, unsafe, partial, opaque, elab/macro, run_cmd or #eval (PermOrder's #eval is a helper outside the proof).

Hidden-weakening hunt: arc embedding emb/res is a bijection onto zero-diagonal matrices and preserves membership, segments and extremality; Adjacent = both vertices, x != y, IsExtreme of the segment, and the endpoint refutes it through the stronger not-IsExtreme statement; IsVertex = Set.extremePoints; Mathlib's IsExtreme here (left endpoint only) is equivalent to the classical definition by symmetry of open segments; IsTour = tourMatrix of an n-cycle with full support, i.e. exactly the directed Hamiltonian cycles; the coverage bridge (exists_cert) uses certs_cover (kernel decide: certificate cyclic orders = List.permutations' [1..7]) with mem_permutations' and the orbit of 0 under the cycle; chk soundness (ASEPBridge) needs XN_tight (kernel decide: every tight S in range is one of the 8 listed cuts). No weakening found.

Reviewer's own restatement (lean-review/RVRestate.lean): RV.P (indicator sums over all arcs, |S|+2 <= n), RV.IsFace (textbook valid-inequality face), RV.Adj, RV.Tour (cyclic listing f 0 -> ... -> f (n-1) via finRotate), RV.Conjecture1 for every n >= 4. Proved RV.P n = ASEP.arcPolytope n, textbook faces are extreme, every RV.Tour is an ASEP.IsArcTour, tours exist, RV.conjecture1_false : not RV.Conjecture1 and RV.counterexample. Strict build; axioms only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Negative controls: RVNegOk compiles (kernel decide shows chk = false for three digit mutations of a stored certificate and for a certificate paired with another tour's order; dropping a tight cut breaks the coverage fact; positive control chk = true). RVNegFail fails as required ('decide proved that the proposition ... is false').

Non-fresh leanchecker and fresh rebuilds of all local modules passed.

findings: No refutation, discussion or follow-up of Conjecture 1 was found. arXiv:2506.10671 has only v1. The authors' later works checked in full text are arXiv:2511.05045 (Sosso-Bernardelli-Gualandi), arXiv:2507.07003 (Villa-Vercesi-Barta-Mastrolilli), the 2026 Optimization Online 'An Asymptotic Framework for the Integrality Gap of the TSP' (Barta-Mastrolilli-Vercesi-Villa) and E. Vercesi's Pavia/USI doctoral dissertation (iris.unipv.it). None mentions Conjecture 1 or tour neighbourhoods.

Closest known analogue (must be cited): Laurent and Poljak (1992) conjectured that every fractional vertex of the metric polytope met_n is adjacent to an integral vertex (a cut), the 'dominating set conjecture'. Deza and Indik refuted it with an explicit vertex of met_9 adjacent only to fractional vertices (arXiv:math/0512493; Optim. Lett. 1 (2007) 163-169; body read). The ASEP result is the same phenomenon for a different polytope: new as a statement, but not a new type of phenomenon.

No known vertex of a subtour relaxation (symmetric SEP or ASEP) adjacent to no tour was found. Related but non-implying literature: Padberg-Rao diameter-2 results for ATSP/assignment polytopes and Trubin quasi-integrality concern edges between integral vertices, and say nothing about whether every fractional vertex has an integral neighbour.
unread: Laurent-Poljak 1992 original paper; Deza-Indik published version (only the arXiv body was read)
Elliott-Magwood thesis (uOttawa) and Boyd-Elliott-Magwood vertex papers (RIMS Kokyuroku Bessatsu B23); Boyd's subtour-vertex data pages
Citation indices (Semantic Scholar/Crossref 429 per task; not retried; Google Scholar not tried); the 2024 Optimization Online version main-1.pdf (404)
Literature on fractional matching or stable-set polytope adjacency to integral vertices (searched in general terms only)
objections: D-1: The manuscript and significance case must cite Laurent-Poljak and Deza-Indik as the direct precedent. The ASEP counterexample is an instance of a known phenomenon, which tempers novelty-of-kind.

reasons: For: it is an explicit, exactly verified and kernel-checked refutation of a conjecture stated verbatim in the source, with no prior refutation found. It is not a wording, domain or endpoint correction (the polytope, adjacency and tour notions are the source's own), and not a routine corollary of anything in the source.

For: it defeats the source's stated motivation. By Lemmas 4 and 7, the orbit of x* is absent from every tour's neighbourhood, so 'solely pivoting on an integer vertex' cannot reach the full V-description of P_ASEP^8.

Against: the conjecture comes from preliminary tests in a computational OR paper and is a side remark. The tests were exhaustive only for n = 4, 5 and partial at n = 6, and the failure appears at n = 8. A heuristic walk found zero-count vertices 'quickly' at n = 8. The vertex graph is connected anyway, so only the one-step strategy fails.

Against: the Laurent-Poljak to Deza-Indik precedent shows that 'every fractional vertex is adjacent to an integral vertex' conjectures are known to fail beyond small n, so the outcome is unsurprising in kind.

Net: it meets the campaign floor as a genuine first refutation of an identified MathDB conjecture in its exact scope, but its significance is modest. Root may reasonably treat it as the weakest kind of eligible result; I would not oppose a HOLD on significance alone.

368807.recommendation: Correctness, source fidelity and the Lean formalisation hold up under adversarial review (gates A-C PASS). Prior-art search is bounded but clean apart from the Deza-Indik analogue (D PASS bounded). Significance is QUALIFIED_PASS. Eligible for root acceptance subject to root's significance judgment, a paper that cites the Laurent-Poljak/Deza-Indik precedent and notes the Table 2 discrepancy, and root's own extracted replay.
next_actions: Root: adjudicate significance (QUALIFIED_PASS vs HOLD) in light of the Deza-Indik precedent and the side-remark status of the conjecture.
Manuscript: cite Laurent-Poljak 1992 and Deza-Indik 2007; state ordinary adjacency and why the pivot reading coincides; report the Table 2 (b)/(c) discrepancy neutrally; keep n = 7 explicitly open.

Optional: a leanchecker --fresh of ASEPArcs in a larger, explicitly authorised budget; an exhaustive or stronger n = 7 search to settle minimality; a check of whether the March 2024 Optimization Online version already stated Conjecture 1 (chronology only).
Root replay: extracted strict rebuild as usual; this review's lean-build/ is a reference, not a substitute.
